title: Audit Explorer: incremental export, cursor-based pagination, saved-query ACLs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a robust, production-grade Audit Explorer export experience that supports large result sets without blowing memory or Incurring long blocking requests. Deliverables: 1) backend streaming/incremental export endpoints for CSV/JSON that work with RBAC v2 checks, 2) cursor-based pagination for the UI and API to allow clients to page arbitrarily through audit results, 3) saved query objects with ACLs (who can view/run/export), 4) UI for export configuration: time window presets, column selection, format, and throttling/size warnings.

Scope: Console viewer and API parity for search + export. Includes server-side streaming + signed temporary export blobs for very large exports (>100k rows). Excludes long-term archival export pipeline (handled by infra team).

Acceptance criteria:
- Users can create, name, and save queries in Audit Explorer and set visibility scopes (private, team, org) controlled by RBAC v2 roles.
- Search results support cursor-based pagination and return stable cursors even if new events arrive; cursors should be compact opaque tokens.
- Export endpoint supports streaming CSV and line-delimited JSON with content-length not required; small exports still return immediate file download.
- Exports larger than threshold return a signed temporary S3 URL with audit event count and checksum; UI surfaces progress and download link.
- Permission checks for viewing or exporting use RBAC v2 authorization layer and are audited.
- Saved queries appear in the saved-query selector and can be starred, edited, and versioned with last-run metadata.

Technical notes & trade-offs:
- Cursor model: implement stable cursor based on (timestamp, tiebreaker id, server-seq) rather than offset to avoid missing/duplicating when new events inserted; cursor encodes filters + cursor position as encrypted token.
- Streaming: use chunked transfer + server backpressure. For very large exports, we generate an async export job that writes line-delimited JSON/CSV to object storage and returns a signed URL. This avoids holding large responses in memory and keeps request timeouts reasonable.
- RBAC: saved-query ACLs stored in metadata table with role/subject tuples. Evaluate whether saved-query owner can delegate edit/export rights or only view. We surface precise denial reasons in UI for clarity.
- Consistency: cursors are eventually consistent; document semantics in help text (strongly consistent for past events up to index threshold; new events after cursor may appear on subsequent pages).

Instrumentation & observability:
- Track metrics: export_request_total, export_job_created, export_bytes_written, export_error_count, cursor_usage_count, saved_query_create/update/delete.
- Add trace spans for export pipeline (search -> stream -> object-store upload).
- Add audit events for: saved-query create/update/delete, export_requested, export_completed, export_failed, saved-query permission changes.

QA & test plan:
- Unit tests for cursor encoding/decoding, permission checks against RBAC v2 matrix, CSV/JSON formatting edge cases (commas, newlines, unicode).
- Integration test: create 150k synthetic audit events, run an export and verify downloadable file contents and checksum match streaming output.
- E2E test: saved-query lifecycle (create, share, run, edit, export), ensure ACLs enforced when user A shares with team B.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag behind console feature "audit_export_v2".
- Beta rollout to 10% of orgs, monitor export_job_created rate and export_error_count for 72h.
- Gradual ramp to 100% and remove flag after 2 weeks of stable metrics.

Rollback criteria:
- >0.5% export_error_count over a daily window AND >1% of export jobs failing for size >10MB.
- Any RBAC mismatch that allows unauthorized export should trigger immediate rollback.

Open questions:
- Permission model for saved queries: should team admins be able to claim ownership? (UX vs security trade-off)
- Export retention policy for signed URLs (7 days?) and cleanup cadence.

comments: 2026-02-13 Aisha Patel: Spun up initial design doc and prototype of export modal. Opted for server-side async job for >100k rows to avoid timeouts.
2026-02-20 Marco Chen: Backend contract proposed - GET /api/v1/audit/search returns cursor and partial results; POST /api/v1/audit/exports starts an export job accepting cursor and filters.

2026-03-01 Security Review (Lina Borges): RBAC v2 checks must be applied at job creation time and re-validated at download time for delayed jobs. Added requirement to log exporter subject in audit event.
2026-03-05 QA (Diego Ruiz): Integration test scaffold can generate 200k synthetic events; initial run showed memory spike in worker - changed stream buffer sizing to 64KB chunks.
2026-03-08 Product (Nirali Shah): UX request: add a preset "last 90 days" and quick-column toggles for common export shapes. Added to acceptance criteria.
